# contilab

> contilab is a PyTorch framework for empirical continual learning (lifelong, incremental learning) research on vision and language models. It benchmarks methods against catastrophic forgetting (Naive, Joint, EWC, LwF, Experience Replay, DER++, A-GEM, LoRA-per-task), compares them with train-then-consolidate pipelines (Task Arithmetic, TIES-Merging, multi-teacher distillation, teacher-to-student continual distillation), and computes 30+ metrics after training with bootstrap confidence intervals, exact paired tests and Friedman/Nemenyi critical differences. MIT license.

Key facts:

- Scenarios: task-, class- and domain-incremental. Benchmarks: Split MNIST, Permuted MNIST, Split CIFAR-10, Split CIFAR-100, text5 (AG News, Yelp, Amazon, DBpedia, Yahoo Answers) with Hugging Face language models (Pythia, Qwen2.5).
- Metrics: accuracy matrix, forgetting, backward/forward transfer, stability gap, min-ACC and WC-ACC, linear probes, CKA, dormant neurons, effective rank, task-recency bias, calibration, few-shot recovery, loss barriers, LLM general-ability retention, cost. Raw data are stored, so a metric can be added without retraining.
- Speed: several seeds train at once as one torch.func.vmap ensemble (3.8x the throughput of one seed for an MLP on 4 CPU cores); torch.compile and bf16 per preset.
- CPU study, 12 methods on 6 benchmarks, 324 runs: average ranks Joint 1.0, DER++ 2.3, Experience Replay 4.2, multi-teacher distillation 5.2 (Friedman p = 5.8e-6). On Split MNIST class-incremental: DER++ 0.871, multi-teacher distillation 0.863, Experience Replay 0.858, EWC 0.196, LwF 0.228, Naive 0.196, Joint 0.950 (mean over 6 seeds).
- Findings: regularisation alone (EWC, LwF) stays at the Naive level in class-incremental learning even after tuning; multi-teacher distillation needed validation-tuned settings (0.223 to 0.871 on Split MNIST class-incremental, 6 seeds); teacher-to-student continual distillation stores no experts, and a 2x100 student keeps 98% of the full-size accuracy on Permuted MNIST in 0.34 MB.
- Citation: DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23906803 (Zenodo; all versions, resolves to the latest).
- Install: from source (pip install -e .) or a release wheel from https://github.com/JonPark0/contilab/releases; Python 3.11+, PyTorch 2.

## Docs

- [Getting started](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JonPark0/contilab/main/docs/wiki/Getting-Started.md): install, first run, reading the report
- [Results](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JonPark0/contilab/main/docs/wiki/Results.md): the CPU study, rankings, tuned comparison, findings
- [FAQ](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JonPark0/contilab/main/docs/wiki/FAQ.md): which method to use, scenarios, stability gap, language models, GPUs
- [Methods](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JonPark0/contilab/main/docs/wiki/Methods.md): scenarios and strategies with hyperparameters
- [Merging and distillation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JonPark0/contilab/main/docs/wiki/Consolidation.md): Task Arithmetic, TIES-Merging, multi-teacher and continual distillation
- [Metrics](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JonPark0/contilab/main/docs/wiki/Metrics.md): every metric with formula and reference
- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JonPark0/contilab/main/README.md): overview, quick start, references

## Optional

- [Benchmarks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JonPark0/contilab/main/docs/wiki/Benchmarks.md): datasets, models, CPU and GPU profiles
- [Configuration](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JonPark0/contilab/main/docs/wiki/Configuration.md): profiles, presets, matrices, sweeps
- [Performance](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JonPark0/contilab/main/docs/wiki/Performance.md): vmap ensembles, torch.compile, bf16, measured throughput
- [Extending](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JonPark0/contilab/main/docs/wiki/Extending.md): adding a strategy, metric, benchmark or consolidation method
- [Per-run results (CSV)](https://github.com/JonPark0/contilab/tree/main/docs/assets/results/data): one row per run with all scalar metrics
- [Results dataset on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/jonpark0/contilab-cpu-study): the same CSVs with a dataset card (configs cpu_main, cpu_tuned, cpu_student)
- [Changelog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JonPark0/contilab/main/CHANGELOG.md): what changed in each release
